task.description:
CODE-DESIGNER Step 2 — produce the design artefact for ISS-0084 / PI-09 per CLAUDE.md CODE-DESIGNER section.

## Issue recap
- GH-299 / ISS-0084 / PI-09: provide an operations runbook AND a fail-fast startup assertion that emits a deterministic FATAL line pinned by a test so alerts can match.
- Severity: MINOR (operations/runbook). NOT a code-correctness bug — a documentation+assertion gap.
- Affected areas: src/main.zig + docs/
- Current src/main.zig state: `runApiServer` calls `db_pool.Pool.init` at line 141. There is no "read from postgres_information_schema after connect" check. The current `bootstrap_audit.auditPublicSchema` is intentionally non-fatal.

## Classification
Per templates/lego-catalog.md:
- Documentation → Type E (prose design at src/design/pi-09-operations-runbook.md) — the artefact itself
- Code change → Type E (new assertion + fatal helper) — small, novel, single-call, integrates into an existing module
- Test → Type E prose spec at tests/specs/ISS-0084.md

No Type A/B/C/D parameter files apply. Produce a single src/design/pi-09-operations-runbook.md prose design that covers BOTH the runbook content and the assertion + helper, with the test spec embedded or separated as you see fit.

## Design requirements

### A. Operations runbook
- Path: docs/runbook/OPERATIONS.md (new dir)
- Required sections (per the GH-299 body: 'Document the config the app assumes but does not control'):
  1. Required environment variables (with defaults where applicable and the source-of-truth for each)
     - BPM_DB_URL (or equivalent)
     - BPM_DB_POOL_SIZE (with default)
     - BPM_IDP_BASE_URL, BPM_IDP_ADMIN_CREDENTIALS_REF
     - BPM_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN
     - BPM_ENV (production|development)
     - BPM_LOG_LEVEL
     - Any BPM_UAT_TOKEN, BPM_TEST_* that the server reads at boot
  2. Recommended defaults + what each variable controls
  3. Startup sequence ordering (env-parsing -> IDP bootstrap -> Pool.init -> public-schema audit -> fail-fast DB assertion -> provisionTenantSchema -> API server start)
  4. The exact FATAL line emitted on fail-fast (so alerts can match it):
     - Format must be a single line of structured JSON or a stable plaintext matching `FATAL startup.database <message>` so log regexes work
     - Include the variable name and current value (not secret) when applicable
  5. Recovery steps per failure mode
  6. Process management (signal handling, graceful shutdown)
  7. Health-check endpoints + what they assert
  8. References to other docs (link to architecture doc, threat model, agents/ for incident response playbook)

### B. Fail-fast startup assertion in src/main.zig
- Add a function `assertDatabaseConfiguration(allocator, pool) !void` in src/main.zig (or a new file src/operations/startup_assertions.zig if better separation)
- Call it from `runApiServer` IMMEDIATELY after `db_pool.Pool.init` returns successfully and BEFORE `provisionTenantSchema` or any other migration-dependent code runs.
- On failure: log a single FATAL line via `obs_logger.log(allocator, .ERROR, ...)` with the literal prefix `startup.database` and a stable, machine-parseable message field; then `std.process.exit(78)` (sysexits.h EX_CONFIG) so process supervisors and containers see a deterministic exit code.
- Assertion must verify at minimum:
  - `SELECT current_setting('server_version')` returns a string starting with the minimum PostgreSQL major version (currently 14; document this in the runbook too)
  - The current user (`current_user`) has CREATE privilege on the database (so migrations can run); check via `SELECT has_database_privilege(current_user, current_database(), 'CREATE')`
  - `public.schema_migrations` table exists (or assert that the migrations directory has applied all files; the `runMigrations` step will create the table if missing, so this check may need to go AFTER migrations — design should clarify ordering)
  - `search_path` does not contain `pg_catalog` LAST (a common misconfiguration that masks schema names; use `SHOW search_path`)

### C. Test pinning the FATAL line (per-issue requirement)
- New test file: tests/unit/ISS-0084-startup-assertion-test.zig (or under tests/integration if it requires DB — design should choose; integration is more realistic, unit is faster)
- Test name: `assertDatabaseConfiguration_emits_deterministic_fatal_on_misconfig`
- Mock the DB error by stubbing the bad privilege check (or use a separate `_for_testing` entry point that the test can drive)
- Assert the captured log line text == the exact string the ops runbook and the alert will match on. This is the "test pinning" the GH-299 body specifies.

### D. Acceptance criteria mapping (the design MUST cover each)
- AC1: docs/runbook/OPERATIONS.md exists and lists every env var the runtime reads
- AC2: The fail-fast call site is documented (file + line) and the call comes after Pool.init and before any data plane operation
- AC3: A test pins the exact FATAL log line text
- AC4: Alert team can match the FATAL line via a stable regex `^\[ERROR\] startup\.database .*` (define the line precisely in the design)
- AC5: Process exit code is 78 (EX_CONFIG) on config-failure fatal
- AC6: zig build exits 0; zig build test exits 0; new test passes

### E. Constraints (hard)
- No secrets in source. Env vars come from os.environ (std.posix.getenv / std.process.getEnvVar).
- The fail-fast path must NOT depend on a logger that itself can fail silently — the log call's failure must be swallowed and the FATAL printed to stderr directly as the LAST resort.
- Type-E design only (no implementation code beyond signatures).

## Output
Produce ONE file: src/design/pi-09-operations-runbook.md following backend_developer_guide.md §6.

Also list a preliminary tests/specs/ISS-0084.md spec skeleton (or attach it as a section of the design doc) describing the test's exact FATAL line capture.

The design must be complete enough that CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR passes and BACKEND-DEV can implement without ambiguity.

No implementation code in the design (per the validator's hard gate). Public function signatures only. Error taxonomy documented. Dependencies listed.

Return:
- artifacts_out: [src/design/pi-09-operations-runbook.md, tests/specs/ISS-0084.md (if separate)]
- summary: a 2-3 sentence description of the chosen approach
- issues: any MAJOR ambiguities you flagged
acceptance_criteria: src/design/pi-09-operations-runbook.md exists and covers all 6 acceptance criteria
tests/specs/ISS-0084.md exists with the FATAL-line capture test specification
No implementation code bodies in the design (signatures + error taxonomy only)
Depends only on existing modules (db_pool, obs_logger) or clearly names new ones
Design flow: env-parse -> IDP -> Pool.init -> assertDatabaseConfiguration -> provisionTenantSchema -> API server
